messages:
Ava: Quick heads-up — p95 tail on /v1/stream-gen spiked after kernel-selector:v2 deploy. saw 80ms -> 240ms on some requests :grimacing:
Diego: any raw numbers / traces?
Ava: here's a small sample from the profiler (can paste full later):
```
streamed-endpoint: p50 35ms p95 240ms p99 380ms
GPU occupancy: 78% -> 45% during partial-decode
avg batch size: 4 -> 2.1
kernel chosen: small-kernel-quant (fallthrough path)
```
Ava: also noticed increased memcpy counts in the kernel path after the change.
Li: my first thought: kernel-selector started preferring a 'fast small' kernel that can't do efficient KV reuse, so partial-decode causes extra copies. we saw similar with the llama-optim path.
Jun: partial-decode scheduling interacts badly with batch formation. if we wait for more tokens to fill a batch we can amortize kernel overhead, but streams want early flushes.
Morgan: can we lower the token-budget target for streamed requests? e.g. target_tokens=8 -> 4 to force earlier flush and smaller kernel runs.
Diego: lowering token_budget might reduce latency for single-streams but could up-cost (more kernels fired). need telemetry.
sre-bot: incident:stream-high-tail created (id=INC-422). alerted 5m ago. linked to kernel-selector:v2 rollout.
Ava: commit that rolled it out: abc1234 -> changed kernel-ranking weights. suspect ranking function used sequence_len histogram differently.
Li: quick experiment idea:
- run microbench on small-kernel with KV cache warm vs cold
- run with partial-decode enabled/disabled
- run with token_budget {4,8,12}
Jun: i can run the bench this afternoon. will post results to the thread. Tentative command:
```
./perf/run_stream_bench --model gpt-small --kernel small-kernel-quant --partial-decode=true --token-budget=4 --warm-kv
```
Diego: i'll add extra counters for memcpy/kv-hits and kernel-switches in the batcher telemetry (PR will be tiny).
Morgan: also can we tweak queue priority: prefer 'stream-early' queue that flushes after Nms or 2 tokens, even if batch not full? that keeps latency predictable.
Ava: we tried 'early-flush queue' before but it had poor throughput; maybe make it dynamic: only enable early-flush when kernel selection expects high-copy kernel.
Li: alternative: adjust kernel-selector to prefer kernels with KV-friendly path when request has warm-KV flag. cheaper than global reweighted ranking.
Jun: initial microbench results (local VM): token_budget=4 gives p95 120ms (vs 240ms), but GPU util down and kernel-count up 2.3x. KV-hit improves slightly when we force early-send because decoded prefixes stay small.
Ava: thanks. can we do a canary: deploy kernel-selector:v2 but with stream_override=prefer-kv=true for 10% traffic? run for 30m and compare p95 and token-cost.
Diego: PR opened: https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/+/PR-482 (adds telemetry + canary flag)
Morgan: I'll author a small runtime toggle: `streaming.early_flush.dynamic=true` which uses kernel telemetry to decide.
Ava: action items:
- Jun: full microbench matrix + logs (today)
- Diego: telemetry + canary flag (PR in review)
- Morgan: runtime toggle + quick canary rollout (tomorrow)
- Li: prototype kernel-selector kv-aware heuristic (next week)
Ava: can everyone react with :eyes: when they ack? I'll coordinate canary windows.
Jun: :eyes:
Diego: :eyes:
Morgan: :eyes:
Li: :eyes:
sre-bot: incident INC-422 status: investigating -> assigned to eng-runtime
Ava: thanks all — leaning toward temporary revert if canary shows cost spike but no latency win.
